column3: E1 - Desire Stall During Data Migration & Integration
column5: A vague, unaddressed fear (commonly headcount) stalls Desire even when Awareness and Knowledge are strong; the fix is a sponsor-delivered, specific response to the named root cause — not a generic reassurance communication.
column6: Prevents a 2-4 week Desire-stall delay from silently extending into Training if left unaddressed; ties directly to CHTR-01 Sponsorship Charter's escalation obligation.

column3: E2 - Divergence Pattern Detected During Testing / Training
column5: 'Trained' and 'capable' are not the same as 'ready' — Knowledge/Ability can be strong while Bridges still reads Ending; a group-level intervention cannot substitute for the individual-focused 1:1 this pattern requires.
column6: Prevents a training-completion report that looks like success while quietly setting up regression once reinforcement attention moves elsewhere.
column7: CHTR-06 (One-to-One Coaching Charter), RULE-008, D31a CHTRACT-0601-0604

column3: E3 - Two-Clock Problem at Cutover & Go-Live
column5: The organizational (Lewin) clock and the emotional (Bridges/Kübler-Ross) clock rarely finish at the same time; when they disagree, keep reinforcement active on the emotional evidence's timeline, not the delivery plan's.
column6: Directly generalizes the 'Manufacturer A' worked example (PRJ-001); protects against declaring Refreeze from the calendar alone.
column7: CHTR-08 (Pulse/Interview Charter), MP-10 Task 4 (Refreeze from evidence)

column5: A sudden localized regression (renewed workaround usage, 'I told you this would happen' commentary) is usually tied to a specific incident, not a general readiness failure — confirm the incident link before reacting broadly.
column6: Avoids over-correcting with a full retraining cycle when a targeted, in-context coaching response addressing the specific incident is sufficient.

column3: E5 - Reinforcement Gap at Sustainment & Closure
column5: Closing a project on schedule with a stalled Reinforcement score doesn't remove the regression risk — it just defers it to whoever inherits the process next; hold the closure call open until 2-3 consecutive healthy checkpoints.
column6: Directly relevant to PRJ-011 (Just-Culture Patient-Safety Program), the seed case with the highest E5 exposure — no forcing deadline at all.

column3: E6 - Cohort Divergence Across Sites or Departments
column5: A single blended, project-level readiness reading can actively mislead a Steering Committee when cohorts (pilot vs. non-pilot sites, departments) are genuinely in different places; disaggregate before every go/no-go decision.
column6: Directly generalizes the 'Health System C' worked example (PRJ-003 / PRJ-009); prevents a strong pilot cohort from masking a weak non-pilot cohort at go/no-go.
column7: D06 KPI-001 (disaggregated view requirement), Phase Gate decision (RULE-013)

column5: An early pilot of the Communication Draft Generator produced tone mismatches for the Meridia clinical audience (too casual for a patient-safety context) until a Project-scoped prompt override was approved.
column6: Directly motivated the D15d Prompt Template Registry design — a global default template is not always appropriate for every audience/sector.
column7: D15d (Prompt Template Registry), CAIUC custom use case pattern

column5: Without an explicit Trainee/Observer/Autonomous staging model, mentees were being declared 'trained' after a single instructor-led session — matching Module 10's known 'attendance vs. capability' gap.
column6: Directly motivated the D31c three-stage progression model with graduated entry/exit criteria and a regression path (Autonomous failure returns to Observer, not Trainee).
column7: D31c (Mentoring Progression Model), RULE-006 (Competency Pass Threshold)
